```{r setup, include=FALSE}
logo_packages <- c("ggplot2", "dplyr", "sf", "terra", "hexSticker", "png")
logo_available <- all(vapply(
  logo_packages,
  requireNamespace,
  logical(1),
  quietly = TRUE
))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  eval = logo_available,
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 5,
  fig.height = 5,
  fig.path = file.path(tempdir(), "spseg-logo-figures/")
)
```

The lettering is the segregation pattern: higher-resource observations
concentrate inside the word **spseg**. The positions are distributed uniformly,
so the word comes from spatial sorting of a continuous covariate, not a greater
density of points. This follows the getting-started vignette's use of fixed
locations and log-normal resources, but adds a typographic sorting target.
Viridis colors represent continuous resource values. This is a graphic design,
not an additional segregation measure.

All drawing happens in R. `hexSticker` supplies the sticker frame; `ggplot2`
draws the dots. A temporary PNG supplies font outlines that are converted to
polygon shapes with terra and sf. No raster text or solid lettering appears in
the final design. The packages
`hexSticker` and `png` are optional and are not needed to run `spseg()`.

```{r missing-packages, echo=FALSE, results='asis', eval=TRUE}
if (!logo_available) {
  cat("Install the optional hexSticker and png packages to render the logo.\n")
}
```

# A word-shaped neighborhood

Render a bold lowercase word on a temporary graphics device, then read which
pixels contain ink. The ordinary sans-serif font avoids downloading a font;
its precise shape can vary slightly across operating systems. The device and
temporary file are cleaned up even if drawing fails.

```{r word-mask}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

word_mask <- function(word = "spseg", width = 1200, height = 500) {
  file <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  on.exit(unlink(file), add = TRUE)
  grDevices::png(file, width = width, height = height, res = 144, bg = "white")
  device <- grDevices::dev.cur()
  on.exit(
    {
      if (device %in% grDevices::dev.list()) grDevices::dev.off(device)
    },
    add = TRUE
  )
  graphics::par(mar = rep(0, 4), family = "sans")
  graphics::plot.new()
  graphics::plot.window(c(0, 1), c(0, 1), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  size <- 0.94 / graphics::strwidth(word, font = 2)
  graphics::text(0.5, 0.5, word, font = 2, cex = size, adj = c(0.5, 0.5))
  grDevices::dev.off(device)
  image <- png::readPNG(file)
  gray <- if (length(dim(image)) == 2L) image else image[,, 1]
  gray < 0.5
}

mask <- word_mask()
```

Turn the ink into polygon shapes, including the holes inside letters. The
polygons occupy the intended lettering rectangle in the logo's planar coordinate
system. They are used to overlay points, not drawn over the finished logo.

```{r letter-shapes}
word_bounds <- c(left = 0.19, right = 1.81, bottom = 0.58, top = 1.58)
letter_raster <- terra::rast(ifelse(mask, 1, NA_real_))
terra::ext(letter_raster) <- terra::ext(
  word_bounds["left"], word_bounds["right"],
  word_bounds["bottom"], word_bounds["top"]
)
terra::crs(letter_raster) <- ""
letter_shapes <- sf::st_as_sf(terra::as.polygons(letter_raster, aggregate = TRUE))
stopifnot(all(sf::st_is_valid(letter_shapes)))

ggplot(letter_shapes) +
  geom_sf(fill = "grey80", colour = NA) +
  coord_sf(datum = NA) +
  theme_void()
```

# Sort a continuous resource distribution

The hexagon is centered at `(1, 1)` with vertices at the top and bottom. A small
inset leaves space between the dots and the frame. The lettering occupies a
central rectangle; sf overlays determine which points fall inside the letters.
As in the getting-started example, draw resources once and assign their sorted
values to locations ordered by a spatial score. A word-shaped preference,
a central peak, a weaker outer rise, and random noise define that score. The
center has the strongest radial preference, followed by a darker intermediate
band and a lighter edge. Letter membership adds a separate utility boost.
Changing the sorting changes where resources appear, not their overall distribution.

```{r dot-resources}
set.seed(2026)
point_count <- 30000L
noise <- 0.18
letter_strength <- 4
center_strength <- 2
center_width <- 0.2
edge_strength <- 1.6
radius <- 0.94

dots <- tibble(
  x = runif(
    2 * point_count,
    1 - sqrt(3) * radius / 2,
    1 + sqrt(3) * radius / 2
  ),
  y = runif(2 * point_count, 1 - radius, 1 + radius)
) |>
  filter(abs(y - 1) <= radius - abs(x - 1) / sqrt(3)) |>
  slice_head(n = point_count)

point_shapes <- sf::st_as_sf(dots, coords = c("x", "y"), remove = FALSE)
in_word <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(point_shapes, letter_shapes)) > 0L

resource_mean <- 10
resource_gini <- 0.55
resource_sd <- sqrt(2) * qnorm((1 + resource_gini) / 2)
resources <- sort(rlnorm(point_count,
  log(resource_mean) - resource_sd^2 / 2, resource_sd))
distance <- with(dots, sqrt((x - 1)^2 + (y - 1)^2)) / radius
radial_utility <- center_strength * exp(-(distance / center_width)^2) +
  edge_strength * distance^6
score <- letter_strength * in_word + radial_utility + noise * rnorm(point_count)
assigned <- numeric(point_count)
assigned[order(score)] <- resources
dots <- dots |>
  mutate(in_word = in_word, utility = score, resources = assigned)

stopifnot(nrow(dots) == point_count, any(dots$in_word), any(!dots$in_word))
stopifnot(identical(sort(dots$resources), resources))

# Bound the display scale, not the actual resource distribution.
colour_cap <- unname(quantile(resources, 0.9))
dots <- dots |> mutate(colour_value = pmin(resources, colour_cap))

dot_plot <- ggplot(dots, aes(x, y, colour = colour_value)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.38, stroke = 0) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "D", limits = c(0, colour_cap)) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(0, 2), ylim = c(0, 2), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
```

# The sticker

The package-name layer is blank because the dots already spell the name.
Specifying the ordinary font families also avoids `hexSticker` enabling its
bundled-font rendering globally. The automatic preview is written only to a
temporary file, not into the source checkout.

```{r sticker, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
sticker_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
logo <- hexSticker::sticker(
  dot_plot,
  package = "",
  p_family = "sans",
  u_family = "sans",
  s_x = 1,
  s_y = 1,
  s_width = 2,
  s_height = 2,
  h_fill = "#101519",
  h_color = "#303940",
  h_size = 0.65,
  filename = sticker_file,
  dpi = 600
)
logo <- logo + theme(plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2, unit = "mm"))
hexSticker::save_sticker(sticker_file, logo, dpi = 600)
```

```{r preview, echo=FALSE, out.width='360px'}
knitr::include_graphics(sticker_file)
```

# Adjust and export

Increase `point_count` for finer stippling, or increase `noise` relative to
`letter_strength` to weaken resource sorting into the word. Change `word_bounds`
to resize or reposition the lettering. `center_strength` and `center_width`
control the central peak; `edge_strength` controls the weaker outer rise.
All dots have the same size and opacity. Color uses actual resource values,
not ranks, so increasing `resource_gini` genuinely changes color contrast by
making the distribution more right-skewed. A rank palette would discard that
effect. For display only, values above the 90th percentile share the brightest
yellow; `dots$resources` remains unchanged. Raise or lower this display threshold
to change how much of the word reaches yellow.

Export is explicit, so knitting never overwrites the package logo. PNG preserves
transparency outside the hexagon; SVG is an optional vector version.

```{r export, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
hexSticker::save_sticker("spseg-hex.png", logo, dpi = 600)
hexSticker::save_sticker("spseg-hex.svg", logo)
```

The [hexSticker documentation](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/hexSticker/html/sticker.html)
describes frame, placement, and export options.
